items.title: 30.7.3 Determining the Structure of a Molecule from 13C NMR

source_refs.note: Topic 30.7.3 with Quick Check 30.7, answered (PDF 213-214); Figure 30.8 is redrawn. The book's conclusion (2-methoxypropane) is reported, with a warning that the printed shifts fit 2-methylpropan-1-ol. Exercises (PDF 214-216) excluded; answers need review.

items: Count the peaks: the number of peaks is the number of carbon environments. A molecule with 5 carbon atoms but only 3 peaks must have 2 pairs of chemically equivalent carbons.
Look at the position of each peak (its chemical shift) to tell whether the carbon is in an alkane, alkene, alkyne, aromatic or carbonyl environment (Table 30.3).
Work out possible structures that fit both the peak information and the molecular formula.

blocks.text: The book's example: a compound C4H10O gives a 13C spectrum with 3 peaks, at 69.0, 30.5 and 19.0 ppm (Figure 30.8), so there are three carbon environments. Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol each have four different carbons and would show four peaks, so neither fits. The book concludes that the compound is 2-methoxypropane, which has three carbon environments.

blocks.title: Check the shifts too
blocks.text: C4H10O has more isomers than the three the book considers. 2-methoxypropane, CH3-O-CH(CH3)2, would show two peaks for carbons bonded to oxygen (about 56 and 72 ppm) and one near 22 ppm, but the printed spectrum has only one peak above 50 ppm and one at 30.5 ppm. The shifts 69.0, 30.5 and 19.0 ppm fit 2-methylpropan-1-ol, (CH3)2CH-CH2-OH, which also has three carbon environments. Flagged for review.

blocks.prompt: Using Figure 30.8, explain why the spectrum does not match butan-1-ol or butan-2-ol.
blocks.explanation: Both CH3CH2CH2CH2OH and CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3 have four different carbon environments and would give four peaks; the spectrum has only three.

blocks.prompt: Which peaks would you expect in the spectra of butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol?
blocks.explanation: Butan-1-ol: the CH2-O carbon at 50-70 ppm (about 62) and three alkyl carbons at 0-50 ppm (about 35, 19 and 14). Butan-2-ol: the CH-O carbon at 50-70 ppm (about 69) and three alkyl carbons (about 32, 23 and 10).

items: Count peaks (environments), read shifts (Table 30.3), fit to the formula.
C4H10O with 3 peaks: not butan-1-ol or butan-2-ol (4 peaks each).
